title: Should Investors Buy Micron Stock Instead of SK Hynix Stock? | MU Stock vs. SKHY Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions.
summary: Parkevtate compares Micron and SK Hynix head to head on revenue, earnings growth, profitability and valuation to pick the better buy. Both sell high-bandwidth memory into AI data centres, where prices are up more than 300% in some cases, shortages persist, customers are signing multi-year agreements, and both are effectively sold out through 2027. Analysts expect earnings per share to grow 55% a year for Micron and 94% a year for SK Hynix. Operating margins are effectively tied at 75% for Micron versus 74.5% for SK Hynix, and returns on invested capital at 89% versus 87% - levels he calls unprecedented for any company he has followed. Both trade at ridiculously cheap valuations, 3.4x and 3.0x forward earnings, because the market expects cyclical margins to collapse when new capacity arrives. He argues that is overblown: long-term contracts with floor prices keep margins above any previous peak, returns on invested capital should stay at least 40% through 2030, and data-centre replacement demand plus future physical AI (driverless cars, robotics) extend the boom. His discounted cash flow fair values are $1,544 for Micron and $262 for SK Hynix against a current price of $124. Both are BUY calls, and Micron is his pick - he owns it and has bought more. Micron reports quarterly results on 17 December 2026.

calls.bull_case: Physical AI (driverless cars, robotics) adds a new demand wave and extends the boom several more years.
calls.bear_case: Cyclical memory - margins eventually collapse when new capacity arrives; triple-digit price rises are not sustainable.
